questions.q: What is an Azure Virtual Network (VNet)?
options: A public network with no isolation from other Azure customers
A physical cable connecting two datacenters
A synonym for a resource group
Your own private, isolated network inside Azure
questions.explain: A VNet is the cloud equivalent of the network you'd build inside an office — Microsoft provides the physical infrastructure, you define the logical network on top.

questions.q: What is a subnet, and why would you divide a VNet into subnets?
options: A subnet is only used to slow down network traffic intentionally
A completely separate VNet with no relationship to the original
A smaller IP address range within a VNet, often used to separate resources by role like web, app, and data tiers
A billing category unrelated to networking
questions.explain: Subnets let you apply different network rules to different parts of your infrastructure instead of treating the whole VNet as one flat space.

questions.q: Why can resources inside the same VNet communicate with each other privately?
options: Only resources in different VNets can ever communicate
They cannot communicate with each other at all inside a VNet
They use private IP addresses, and that traffic never has to go out over the public internet
Because Azure charges extra for public communication, forcing private routing
questions.explain: Private IP addresses within the same VNet (or connected VNets) let resources talk directly without exposing that traffic to the public internet.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the actual point of a VNet — connectivity or isolation?
options: Connectivity — a VNet's only purpose is making resources reachable from the internet
Cost reduction is the sole purpose of a VNet
Neither — a VNet has no security implications at all
Isolation — by default, a VNet is a private space that nothing enters unless explicitly allowed
questions.explain: The default-closed posture — nothing gets in unless explicitly allowed — is what makes a VNet a real boundary you control, not just a network.

questions.q: Why is placing a database in its own subnet, disconnected from the public internet, more secure even before any specific firewall rule is added?
options: Because subnets automatically encrypt all data regardless of configuration
There is no security benefit to using a subnet
Because databases placed in subnets can never be accessed by any resource, even internal ones
Because a VNet and its subnets are private by default, so nothing outside can reach it without being explicitly allowed
questions.explain: The default-closed nature of a VNet/subnet means the database isn't directly reachable from the public internet at all, independent of any additional rule.
